title: Seizure
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with new-onset seizure, altered mental status, autonomic hyperactivity (tachycardia, hypertension, diaphoresis, hyperthermia), tremors, and visual/tactile hallucinations (formication). History reveals chronic heavy alcohol use with abrupt cessation 24-72 hours prior. This is alcohol withdrawal progressing to delirium tremens — a medical emergency with 5-15% mortality if untreated. Pathophysiology: chronic alcohol enhances GABA inhibition and suppresses NMDA glutamate excitation. Abrupt withdrawal → loss of GABA tone + rebound glutamate hyperactivity → CNS hyperexcitability. The CIWA-Ar score quantifies severity and guides treatment. Management: benzodiazepines (diazepam, lorazepam, chlordiazepoxide) — symptom-triggered or fixed-schedule dosing until sedated but arousable. Thiamine before glucose (prevent Wernicke's). IV fluids for dehydration. Correct electrolytes (hypomagnesemia, hypokalemia common). Admit to ICU for severe DTs. Rule out other causes of seizure: CT head, EEG, tox screen, metabolic panel.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Neuro / Psych
stacks.finding: AMS, hallucinations, tremors, hyperreflexia. Seizure activity.

stacks.label: CIWA-Ar scoring
stacks.finding: Quantifies withdrawal severity. Guides benzodiazepine dosing. Score >15 = severe withdrawal.

stacks.label: CBC
stacks.finding: Screening. Anemia, thrombocytopenia common in AUD.

stacks.label: BMP / CMP
stacks.finding: Electrolyte abnormalities — hypomagnesemia, hypokalemia. Check Mg, Phos, K.

stacks.label: Toxicology screen (urine/serum)
stacks.finding: Confirm co-ingestants. Rule out other toxidromes.

stacks.label: CT head without contrast
stacks.finding: New-onset seizure — rule out intracranial hemorrhage, trauma, mass.

stacks.label: EEG
stacks.finding: If seizure vs DT tremor unclear. Rule out non-convulsive status epilepticus.

stacks.label: Thiamine (IV/IM)
stacks.finding: Thiamine BEFORE glucose to prevent Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome.

stacks.label: Benzodiazepine (Diazepam / Lorazepam / Chlordiazepoxide)
stacks.finding: First-line for alcohol withdrawal. Symptom-triggered per CIWA or fixed-schedule. Titrate to sedation but arousable.

stacks.label: IV fluids (NS / LR with electrolytes)
stacks.finding: Dehydration from diaphoresis, poor intake. Correct electrolytes.

stacks.label: Magnesium / Potassium replacement
stacks.finding: Hypomagnesemia and hypokalemia common in AUD — correct.

stacks.label: Admit to ICU
stacks.finding: Delirium tremens requires ICU for continuous CIWA monitoring, IV benzodiazepines, and management of autonomic instability.

physical_exam.neurological: Generalized tremor. Hyperreflexia. Visual hallucinations (formication). Seizure. AMS. CIWA-Ar high.
physical_exam.psychiatric: Visual and tactile hallucinations. Agitation. Paranoia.

decoys.label: Glucose without thiamine first
decoys.reason_wrong: Giving glucose before thiamine in alcoholic/malnourished patients can PRECIPITATE Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome. Always give thiamine first.

decoys.label: Antipsychotics (haloperidol) as monotherapy
decoys.reason_wrong: Antipsychotics lower seizure threshold — dangerous in alcohol withdrawal. Benzodiazepines are first-line. Antipsychotics only as adjunct for severe hallucination/agitation.

teach_me_steps.reasoning: Seizure + AMS + autonomic hyperactivity + hallucinations after alcohol cessation. CIWA-Ar score quantifies severity. 5-15% mortality untreated. GABA withdrawal + glutamate rebound.

teach_me_steps.order: Benzodiazepines: titrate to calm but arousable
teach_me_steps.reasoning: First-line. Diazepam IV or lorazepam IV. Symptom-triggered (per CIWA) or fixed-schedule. Thiamine before glucose. Correct Mg/K. ICU for severe DTs.

case_summary: Delirium tremens: seizure + AMS + autonomic hyperactivity + hallucinations 24-72h after EtOH cessation. CIWA-guided benzodiazepines + thiamine + IVF + Mg/K. ICU admission.
